paper_source_and_normalization.definitions: V(T|P) is conditional proof cost; accepted source-code proof length and ideal shortest-proof value are distinct. L(T|P)=S(T)+sum of statement lengths of definitions in C(T) but not C(P). I=100V/L. For the empty-context correlation, U_0=|D(T)| V(T|empty), where D(T) means direct users. The paper's reported rho=0.756 excludes U_0=0. The local Cartesian V,L,d are synthetic metadata, not reconstructed Lean proofs.

shared_factor_countermodel.surviving_theorem: For uniform (j,d), V=C^j, C>m, constant L=100, I=V and U=dV: I is exactly independent of d, yet rho(I,U)^2=m^2(n^2-1)/(m^2 n^2-1) tends to one. The saved exact check covers 343 (n,m) cases. The varying-length Cartesian witness uses L in {100,200}, d in {1,2,3,4} and V=10^j.
shared_factor_countermodel.exact_400_row_result: At n=50, rho(I,U)^2=44408896/44438889, rho=0.9996624796079071; rho(I,d)=0 and full joint independence holds. Root's independent pairwise-midrank implementation reproduces this and gives the stronger ordinary V-only control rho(V,U)^2=13328/13333, rho=0.999812477730082.
shared_factor_countermodel.zero_use_extension: Adding complete d=0 counterparts preserves the positive-use conditional statistic while the ever-used fraction can approach zero; saved examples give fractions 1, 1/2, 1/10 and 1/100.
shared_factor_countermodel.failed_inference: High I-U correlation alone does not identify reuse-count prediction, fraction ever reused, consequential novelty or improved future discovery. This does not refute I predicting the defined U, library-compression value, the paper's actual empirical results, or its learned model. No actual paper rows were reanalysed.
